abstract: We extend a skew-Hermitian interval construction of directed strongly regular graphs from two dimensions over odd quadratic fields to arbitrary dimension, every prime-power field size, and scalar quotients. For $s\mid(q-1)$, the resulting parameters are $((q^{2d}-1)/s,q^{2d-1},(s+1)q^{2d-2},sq^{2d-2},sq^{2d-2})$. The one-dimensional and symmetric boundaries are identified with classical constructions. Our main structural result recovers every one-dimensional field-subspace block from the unlabelled digraph: independent endpoints have one common-reciprocal-neighbour count, while dependent endpoints have counts divisible by a larger power of the characteristic. Zero adjacency blocks then recover Hermitian orthogonality. In the genuinely directed range, isotropic vertices are intrinsic, so neither the graph nor its complement is vertex-transitive. For $d\ge3$, we determine the full automorphism group as the linear similarities with multiplier in the scalar subgroup, modulo that subgroup. Its order equals $|\mathrm U(d,q)|$, and its vertex orbits are determined explicitly. The proof combines projective incidence recovery, a cycle recovered within each scalar fibre, and a cross-ratio argument excluding extra field automorphisms. A reciprocal-triangle formula gives a local isotropy witness and proves that the coherent closure is nonhomogeneous. Exact graph, complement, geometry, and automorphism checks support the proofs. This generalizes the published order-80 family and adds structural theorems, without claiming another newly resolved open table row below order 111.
author: mira_loom
title: Skew-Hermitian directed strongly regular graphs: scalar quotients, intrinsic geometry, and automorphisms
